title: Assignment of Benefit (AOB)
h1: Assignment of Benefit (AOB) and bulk billing consent
description: Plain-English explanation of Assignment of Benefit and Medicare bulk billing consent at Woolloongabba Medical Centre, including HotDoc requests.
headings: How you may receive an AOB request
text: Patient Information Assignment of Benefit (AOB) and bulk billing consent For eligible Medicare bulk billed services, patients assign their Medicare benefit to the practice. You may be asked to confirm that consent by HotDoc message, email or notification. Explore related pages Received a consent request? Respond promptly so bulk billing for an eligible consult can be completed. Book Appointment Call Clinic What Assignment of Benefit means Assignment of Benefit (AOB) is the Medicare process where you agree that the Medicare benefit for an eligible service is paid to the practice. In plain terms, it is the consent that lets bulk billing work for that consultation or service when Medicare rules allow it. This page explains practice process only. It is not financial or legal advice, and Medicare rules can change. Why consent is required Medicare expects patient consent before a bulk billed claim can be lodged for an eligible service. Completing AOB confirms your details and your agreement that the benefit is assigned to the practice for that care. Woolloongabba Medical Centre provides 100% Medicare bulk billing for standard Medicare-eligible general practice consultations for patients with a valid Medicare card. Some services sit outside standard Medicare billing — see Bulk Billing and Medicare . How you may receive an AOB request After an appointment, or sometimes before, you may receive a consent request. Requests may be sent via HotDoc as SMS or email. You may also see HotDoc app notifications related to consent. Please respond promptly so billing for an eligible bulk billed service can be completed. A legitimate request asks you to confirm consent details — it does not ask for banking passwords or account logins. If a message looks wrong Call (07) 3217 3344 before completing anything. See Identifying HotDoc scam messages for domain and safety checks. Assignment of Benefit questions What does Assignment of Benefit mean? Assignment of Benefit means you agree that Medicare can pay the benefit for an eligible service directly to the practice, instead of paying you first. That is how bulk billing usually works for Medicare-eligible GP consultations at our clinic. Why is consent required? Medicare requires patient consent (Assignment of Benefit) so the practice can claim the Medicare benefit for an eligible bulk billed service. Without consent, the claim pathway for that service may not be completed. Bulk billing → How will I receive an AOB or consent request? You may receive a short HotDoc SMS or email, or a HotDoc notification, asking you to confirm your details for Medicare consent. Requests can arrive before or after an appointment. What should I do when I get a request? Open the legitimate HotDoc link and complete the consent steps promptly. If you are unsure the message is genuine, call the clinic before responding. We will not ask for banking passwords. Book Appointment Related information Bulk Billing → Medicare → Booking & HotDoc → This page provides general information about Medicare bulk billing consent at our practice. It is not financial or legal advice. For your personal Medicare entitlements, check with Services Australia or ask reception about our current billing pathways.

title: Medicare Exclusions
description: Understand non-Medicare services including employment and driver medicals, insurance reports and other private-fee appointments.
text: Fees & Medicare Medicare Exclusions A clear guide to services that may attract a private fee because they are outside standard Medicare-funded general practice care. Fees & Medicare Some services sit outside Medicare. Woolloongabba Medical Centre provides 100% Medicare bulk billing for standard Medicare-eligible general practice consultations for patients with a valid Medicare card. Some services are provided for employment, licensing, insurance, reporting or other non-Medicare purposes and can attract a private fee. Common Medicare exclusions Pre-employment medicals — assessments requested for employment or workplace purposes, including a WorkCover or work injury medical. Driver medicals — including commercial driver medical assessments and other licensing-related medicals. Insurance reports — insurance medicals, insurance forms, certificates or other information prepared for insurers or other third parties. Other non-Medicare services — services that are not eligible for a Medicare benefit, including some reports, forms, procedures and administrative medical work. Fees may apply. Contact reception for pricing details before your appointment. Where a private fee applies, the practice aims to explain the charge in advance wherever practical. Before you book Tell reception what the medical, form or report is for. This helps the team arrange the right appointment length and tell you what documents to bring. Some assessments require specific forms, identification, reports or testing. Read about medical assessments and procedures → Patient questions Frequently Asked Questions Are all services at the practice covered by Medicare? No. Standard Medicare-eligible general practice consultations may be bulk billed, but some services are outside Medicare and attract a private fee. Are pre-employment medicals covered by Medicare? Pre-employment medicals, including a WorkCover or work injury medical, are generally undertaken for employment or administrative purposes rather than treatment of an illness and may attract a private fee. Do driver medicals attract a fee? Driver and commercial driver medical assessments may be non-Medicare services and may attract a private fee. Contact reception before booking for current pricing and appointment requirements. Are insurance reports covered by Medicare? Insurance reports, insurance medicals, insurance forms and other reports prepared for third parties are generally not standard Medicare-funded consultations and may attract a private fee. Related information Fees & Billing → Bulk Billing → Medicare → Contact Reception →

title: Medicare
description: Find Medicare card, rebate and bulk-billing information for Woolloongabba Medical Centre, with official resources.
text: Patient Information Medicare A simple guide to Medicare cards, rebates, updating your information and useful official resources. Information for patients of Woolloongabba Medical Centre in Brisbane’s inner south. At your appointment Please bring your current Medicare card or Medicare number and any relevant concession card. We use this information to confirm billing eligibility and process eligible Medicare rebates electronically at reception where applicable. Medicare and your appointment Medicare is Australia’s universal health care system. If you are enrolled, Medicare may cover some or all of the cost of eligible health services. Bring your Medicare card or Medicare number to your appointment so we can confirm your details and billing eligibility. Your Medicare card If your card is lost, stolen, damaged or expired, Services Australia allows you to request a replacement through your Medicare online account linked to myGov or through the myGov app. A digital Medicare card can also be available through myGov. If your address or contact details change, update them with Medicare and let reception know so we can keep your practice record current. Medicare rebates If a service is bulk billed, Medicare pays the provider directly and there is no Medicare rebate for you to claim separately for that service. If you pay privately for an eligible service, we may be able to submit an electronic Medicare claim on your behalf, or you can claim through Medicare. Bring your current Medicare card or Medicare number and any relevant concession card so we can confirm your details and billing eligibility. What happens when a service is bulk billed? When an eligible service is bulk billed, Medicare pays the provider directly and there is no separate Medicare rebate for you to claim for that service.
